backlog.spec: In half of the perturbation trials (rng.random() < 0.5), perturb only the circles that are loosely held in the best packing. Compute for each circle its number of contacts: pairs with centre distance minus the two radii below 1e-4, plus walls with clearance minus radius below 1e-4. Take the 5 circles with the fewest contacts, ties broken by smaller radius, and add centre noise with sd 0.08 to them only; the other centres stay unchanged. Start radii are 0.5 times the best radii for all circles as now. Run SLSQP, repair and accept as usual. The other half of the trials use the current uniform jitter.
backlog.title: Target the loosest circles: jitter only low-contact circles

backlog.spec: Add an `ftol` argument to _solve_once and pass it into the SLSQP options. Fresh random starts keep the scipy default, 1e-6. Perturbed starts use ftol = 1e-9, with MAX_ITER unchanged at 200. With the default tolerance SLSQP can stop about 1e-4 to 1e-3 short of the local optimum in sum of radii, which is the size of the gap between the current result and the best known value. This is not a separate final polish stage: only the tolerance of the existing perturbation solves changes, and no extra time is reserved.
backlog.title: Tighter SLSQP ftol for perturbed starts

backlog.spec: Combine slots 29 and 7. Fresh random restarts (the first 30% of the time) start from row-structured hex-like starts: 5 or 6 rows with a random number of circles per row adding up to 26, evenly spaced in each row, with uniform jitter of 0.02 and initial radius 0.05. In the perturbation phase, half the time remove the 3 smallest circles of the best packing and reinsert them at random uniform positions in [0.1, 0.9]^2 with radius 0.02, while the other circles keep their centres and get radii x0.5. The other half of the time, use the existing jitter perturbation.
backlog.title: Remove-3-smallest combined with row-hex starts

backlog.spec: In the perturbation phase, with probability 0.4, pick a random circle whose radius lies between the 30th and 70th percentile of the best packing. Move its centre to the point with the largest clearance: evaluate a 60x60 grid over [0.02, 0.98]^2 and take the point that maximises min(distance to wall, min_j(dist to c_j - r_j)), excluding the moved circle. Give all circles radii x0.5, add jitter with sd 0.003 and run SLSQP. Otherwise use the existing perturbation.
backlog.title: Relocate one random mid-size circle to the largest hole

backlog.spec: For fresh random restarts, replace rng.uniform for the centres with a 2-D Halton sequence (bases 2 and 3) over [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW]. Use a per-call offset drawn from rng so that different seeds give different, but still well-spread, point sets. Keep the initial radii at INIT_RADIUS and everything else unchanged. The point is to cover the square more evenly than iid uniform draws, with no extra SLSQP cost.
backlog.title: Halton low-discrepancy random-restart starts

backlog.spec: Pass bounds to SLSQP: centres in [0,1] and radii in [0,0.25], and remove the redundant constraint r>=0 from cons. This shrinks the constraint vector and keeps the iterates sane. Leave the rest unchanged.
backlog.title: Variable-bound SLSQP

backlog.spec: For fresh random starts, draw 26 uniform points in the unit square and apply 5 Lloyd iterations using a 60x60 grid of sample points (assign each grid point to the nearest site, move each site to the centroid of its cells). Use the result as centres with initial radius 0.05. Gives evenly spread starts without extra libraries.
backlog.title: Lloyd-relaxed random starts

backlog.spec: For half of the fresh random restarts, place the n circle centres on 3 concentric rings around the square centre (0.5, 0.5). Assign each ring a count drawn from rng (roughly 1 central, 8 middle, 17 outer, with random jitter of plus or minus 2 per ring, summing to n). Put points evenly on each ring with a random phase in [0, 2*pi). Add Gaussian noise with sd 0.02 to each centre, clip to [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW], and set initial radii to INIT_RADIUS. The other half of the restarts stay uniform.
backlog.title: Concentric-ring random starts

backlog.spec: In solve, replace rng.choice([0.005, 0.01, 0.02, 0.05]) with a weighted choice. Keep a weight array w = ones(4) for the four sd values. After each perturbation run, if the result beats the best, add 1 to the weight of the sd that was used. Choose sd with probability w / w.sum(). The restart phase and everything else stay unchanged.
backlog.title: Adaptive perturbation sd by success counts

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, when start is given, build the starting radii as start[1] * rng.uniform(0.3, 0.9, n), so each circle gets its own shrink factor, instead of the fixed start[1] * 0.5. Keep the centre jitter, the sd choices, the 30% switch point and everything else unchanged.
backlog.title: Random radius shrink factor in perturbation

backlog.spec: In solve, during the perturbation phase (after 30% of the time), use this start half the time (rng.random() < 0.5): take the best packing, pick a random circle k, set its starting radius to 1.6 * r_k and every other radius to 0.9 * r, and add centre jitter with sd 0.005. Run SLSQP from that start; this pushes the packing into a nearby basin. Add an optional radius-factor argument to _solve_once, or build x0 in solve and pass it in. The other half of the time, use the existing perturbation. Repair and keep-best as now.
backlog.title: Inflate-one-circle perturbation

backlog.spec: In the perturbation phase, replace the uniform rng.choice over [0.005, 0.01, 0.02, 0.05] with an adaptive choice. Keep two arrays of length 4, tries and wins, initialised to 1 and 1. For each trial pick index k with probability proportional to wins / tries (normalise and pass as p to rng.choice), run the perturbed solve with that sd, then increment tries[k] and, if the result improved the best sum of radii by more than 1e-7, increment wins[k]. Everything else stays the same. This moves trials towards the noise scale that is producing improvements in this run.
backlog.title: Bandit choice of perturbation sd by success counts

backlog.spec: In the perturbation phase, keep a counter `fails` of consecutive trials that did not improve the best; reset it to 0 on improvement. While fails < 6, draw sd from [0.005, 0.01, 0.02] as a mild search. When fails >= 6, use an escalated move for that trial: sd = 0.05 on all centres, and in addition replace the centres of the 2 smallest circles with uniform random points in [0.1, 0.9]^2 before the solve. After one escalated trial set fails to 3, so that mild trials run again before the next escalation. Acceptance is unchanged: keep the result only if the sum of radii improves.
backlog.title: Escalate to larger moves only after stagnation

backlog.spec: In the perturbation branch of _solve_once, scale each circle's centre noise by its size: sd_i = sd * clip(sqrt(mean(r) / max(r_i, 1e-3)), 0.5, 3.0), where r is start[1]. Small circles move more and large circles move less. Draw the noise as rng.normal(0, 1, (n, 2)) * sd_i[:, None]. Keep the radii x0.5 and everything else unchanged.
backlog.title: Radius-scaled centre jitter

backlog.spec: For a fraction (about 40%) of fresh random restarts, first solve the packing for n+1 circles with the same SLSQP and _repair, starting from uniform random centres. Then delete the circle with the smallest radius, and run SLSQP once more on the remaining n circles, starting from those centres and radii times 0.5. Compare the final result with the normal restart result and keep the better. The aim is to start from a packing that has room to spare, then remove the weakest circle to get a different basin.
backlog.title: Grow to 27 circles then drop the smallest

backlog.spec: In the perturbation phase, replace the single isotropic centre noise with a two-level noise. For each trial draw a random mask where each circle is selected with probability 0.2 (force at least 2 selected). Selected circles get centre noise with sd 0.06, the others get sd 0.003. Implement it by passing a per-circle sd array of shape (n, 1) to _solve_once, which numpy broadcasts in rng.normal(0, sd, start[0].shape). Use this sparse noise in half of the perturbation trials, chosen with rng.random() < 0.5, and the existing uniform sd choice in the other half. Radii start at 0.5 times the best radii as now. The selection is by random index, not by spatial region.
backlog.title: Sparse heavy-tailed jitter: a few circles move far, the rest barely

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, the perturbed start currently uses start[1] * 0.5 for the radii. Add a parameter `shrink` (default 0.5) and use start[1] * shrink. In solve, during the perturbation phase, draw shrink = rng.choice([0.5, 0.7, 0.85, 0.95]) independently of the centre sd and pass it in. Change nothing else. The aim is that milder shrinks keep the contact structure, so SLSQP converges faster and does finer local search, while 0.5 remains available for larger rearrangements.
backlog.title: Randomise the radius shrink factor in the perturbation phase

backlog.spec: In the perturbation phase, keep a counter of consecutive children that fail to improve the best radius sum. When the counter reaches 15, discard the perturbation chain and start a fresh uniform random SLSQP restart, which becomes the new current packing, and reset the counter. Otherwise, perturb the best as in slot 2 (radii x0.5, centre sd drawn from [0.005, 0.01, 0.02, 0.05]). This avoids spending the rest of the time in one basin when the perturbations have stalled.
backlog.title: Stagnation-triggered reseed in the perturbation phase

backlog.spec: Set the random-restart phase to 20% of the time limit (instead of 30%). In the perturbation phase, always use the slot-29 style move on the best packing with probability 0.5: remove the 3 smallest circles, place them at random positions with radius 0.02, and re-optimise; otherwise use the existing jitter with radii x0.5. Both start from the best packing.
backlog.title: Restart phase 20% with remove-3-smallest reinsertion

backlog.spec: In the perturbation phase (after 30% of the time), build each child by scaling all centres about their common centroid by a factor s ~ U(0.97, 1.03), adding a small Gaussian jitter (sd 0.005) to the centres, and resetting radii to 0.5 times the best radii as in slot 2. Then run the same SLSQP and _repair. Leave the restart loop, the elite choice (keep the single best) and TIME_FRACTION unchanged. The scale move is a global, non-Gaussian change of spacing that the existing jitter does not produce.
backlog.title: Global scale perturbation of the best packing

memo: Helped: only slot 2 (30% of time on random restarts, then perturb the best packing with radii x0.5 and re-optimise), -2.6349, one run, unconfirmed given noise sd 0.0023. Slot 29 (remove 3 smallest circles and reinsert) gave the best raw value, -2.6360, but was rejected against the incumbent's adjusted measure. Slots 6, 7, 16, 18 and 27 reached -2.6354, within noise of slot 2. Did not help: LP radii, swaps, relocating small circles (-2.6249), analytic Jacobians, screening, wall-biased, Latin hypercube, mirrored and random-radii starts, higher time fraction, basin hopping, pruning, long final polish, crossover, rotate/translate (-2.6275). Start-distribution and solver changes mostly hurt. Next: replicate slots 2, 16 and 29 to confirm the -2.635 level, since single runs are noisy. Tune the restart fraction (20% vs 50%) and perturbation size. Try repeated perturb-and-reoptimise cycles. Combine slot 29 with slot 6 or 7 starts. Avoid already-tried ideas (several were aborted as duplicates).
